throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: x86rotr.w $r12, $r4; x86rotr.w $r13, $r5; x86rotr.w $r14, $r6; x86rotr.w $r15, $r7; x86rotr.w $r16, $r8; x86rotr.w $r17, $r9; x86rotr.w $r18, $r10; x86rotr.w $r19, $r11
throughput.init: addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8; x86mtflag $r0, 1
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'addi.d $r4, $r0, 1; addi.d $r5, $r0, 2; addi.d $r6, $r0, 3; addi.d $r7, $r0, 4; addi.d $r8, $r0, 5; addi.d $r9, $r0, 6; addi.d $r10, $r0, 7; addi.d $r11, $r0, 8; x86mtflag $r0, 1' --asm 'x86rotr.w $r12, $r4; x86rotr.w $r13, $r5; x86rotr.w $r14, $r6; x86rotr.w $r15, $r7; x86rotr.w $r16, $r8; x86rotr.w $r17, $r9; x86rotr.w $r18, $r10; x86rotr.w $r19, $r11'
throughput.notes: The instruction writes no general-purpose register, so the 8 lanes differ in their source registers and each one retires an EFLAGS write; 16.00 cycles for 8 instructions is the flag-write throughput, 2 CPI (0.5 IPC).

notes: LBT x86-style instruction. rd is both source and destination. Latency is recorded per source operand: the rd accumulator path, the rk path, and the EFLAGS path. Only EFLAGS is written: the general-purpose registers are read-only sources for this instruction (verified with a native test program, where every GPR keeps its value after execution while EFLAGS changes as documented, e.g. x86sub.b of 6 and 7 sets CF, SF, PF and AF).
